title: Microscopic Spin-1 Parent Hamiltonians for Emergent Valence-Bond Loop Manifolds
authors: Hari Borutta, Yasir Iqbal, Kirill Shtengel
abstract: We construct an exact spin-$1$ parent Hamiltonian for constrained valence-bond loop manifolds on the checkerboard and pyrochlore lattices. The Hamiltonian is local, SU(2)- and time-reversal-invariant, and built from positive-semidefinite projectors acting on triangular faces. Each projector removes only the maximally polarized state of a triangle, so the model is frustration-free. Its zero-energy states are generated by an AKLT-like construction in which each spin-$1$ moment is resolved into two virtual spin-$\tfrac12$ degrees of freedom, singlets are formed inside every crossed plaquette or tetrahedron, and the physical spin-$1$ Hilbert space is recovered by projection. The resulting ground states are fully packed singlet-loop states on the corner-sharing lattice. Thus, a loop or dimer constraint, usually introduced as part of an effective Rokhsar--Kivelson description, appears here as the exact zero-energy manifold of a microscopic spin Hamiltonian. We analyze spin correlations within this manifold and show that, for a fixed loop covering, they are determined by loop connectivity. We also project symmetry-allowed perturbations into the ground-state manifold and derive the resulting low-energy pseudospin dynamics. The checkerboard and pyrochlore cases differ sharply. On the pyrochlore lattice, tetrahedral symmetry removes simple local bias terms, and the leading nontrivial next-nearest-neighbour Heisenberg perturbation gives an emergent spin-$\tfrac12$ XY model on the diamond lattice of tetrahedron centers. These results give an exact spin-$1$ microscopic starting point for constrained valence-bond physics in two and three dimensions, and show how loop, dimer, and gauge-theoretic descriptions can be approached from a small-spin, SU(2)-invariant frustrated magnet.
summary: This paper constructs an exact, local, SU(2)-invariant parent Hamiltonian using spin-1 moments on frustrated lattices. It demonstrates that the ground state manifold naturally encodes loop constraints characteristic of valence-bond physics. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding quantum magnetism in 2D and 3D systems.
main_problem: To determine if constrained valence-bond loop manifolds can arise exactly as the ground-state space of a local, microscopic SU(2)-invariant spin Hamiltonian.
main_result: The construction provides an exact spin-1 parent Hamiltonian for these frustrated systems, showing that loop constraints emerge naturally from the zero-energy manifold.
method: The authors use an AKLT-inspired fractionalization procedure and project symmetry-allowed perturbations into the resulting ground-state manifold to derive low-energy dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is a spin-1 Hamiltonian defined on checkerboard and pyrochlore lattices, constructed using projectors acting on triangular faces. It aims to capture physics related to valence-bond loops in frustrated magnets.
key_observables: Spin correlations within the ground state manifold (determined by loop connectivity) and effective low-energy pseudospin dynamics (e.g., emergent XY model terms).
important_parameters: The coupling constant J, and the lattice structure (checkerboard vs. pyrochlore).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that projecting perturbations into the ground state manifold captures the low-energy physics, and specific mathematical lemmas are used to establish the local kernel structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the checkerboard and pyrochlore lattices, showing where the projector acts on triangular faces. Other figures detail the AKLT-like construction using virtual spin-1/2 singlets.
paper_structure: The paper first constructs the microscopic Hamiltonian ($H_0$) via projectors. It then analyzes the zero-energy manifold using fractionalization techniques and proves its connection to loop states. Finally, it calculates matrix elements of perturbations within this manifold to derive effective low-energy Hamiltonians for different lattice types.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous, microscopic starting point (spin-1) for studying complex constrained quantum phases like valence-bond solids, bridging concepts from spin models, dimer coverings, and gauge theories.
